overview: A series of systems crosses the West this week. Coast Mountains and Cascades get repeated snow and rain through Wednesday. The Rockies get lighter, mostly drier spells, with snow chances on Monday and again later in the week. The Northeast sees a stronger storm late in the week.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: The main thing here is a stretch of wet weather. Showers and a wave of steadier precipitation arrive Monday, with more rain and wind through Wednesday. Snow levels sit fairly high, so the snow is mostly confined to upper elevations. Whistler leads with about 75" on the radar, and its peak day is Tuesday, when about 22" falls.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A stronger front moves in Tuesday into Wednesday as an upper low deepens offshore, bringing widespread rain and mountain snow with snow levels near 3,000 to 3,500 feet. Rain is heaviest Wednesday night into Thursday, and the Skokomish River may rise to flood stage. The best snow comes Thursday, when Mt. Baker sees its biggest day.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: A coastal storm spreads heavy rain and strong winds up the East Coast Wednesday and Thanksgiving. Some snow develops in the Central Appalachians and interior Northeast Thursday into Friday, with windy rain and snow showers lingering in New England. Friday is the peak day at Blue Mountain and Le Massif.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Light snow and flurries come and go through the week, with a more organized wave Wednesday night and Thursday. Thursday is the best day, with rain mixing in at lower elevations. Revelstoke has the biggest totals in the region.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Mostly quiet, with cold, dry spells Tuesday and Wednesday. A quick Monday system brings only light snow to the western mountains. A stronger wave arrives around Thanksgiving, with snow showers likely Thursday. Grand Targhee and Jackson Hole see their best snow Friday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Cold and mostly dry, with a short window of mountain snow showers late Monday into Tuesday morning. Snow chances return Thanksgiving week, with Friday the best day at Breckenridge and Steamboat. The timing is still uncertain, and forecasters expect no major travel impacts over the holiday.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Mostly flurries and showers, with little snow at the resorts. Thursday brings the most precipitation, and it falls more as rain than snow at lower elevations. Big White has the largest total in the region.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
